$comment: The single list of which skills are active on this machine.
Nothing here is ever deleted. 'parked' means the skill stays installed but is
unlinked from the agent directories, so it costs no description tokens and
competes with nothing. Flip a value and re-run apply-registry.sh to change
your mind — re-activating is instant and works offline.
Why park anything: every active skill's name + description is loaded into
context at the start of EVERY session. At 167 active skills that was ~12,000
tokens before typing a word, and a dozen skills competing for the same
trigger, which makes the model's choice arbitrary rather than informed.
mine        skills in claude-code/skills/ — bootstrap.sh reads this
thirdParty  skills in ~/.agents/skills/  — apply-registry.sh reads this
Anything installed but absent from this file defaults to ACTIVE, so a new
`npx skills add` works without editing anything first.

parked.industrial-brutalist-ui: one of six taste skills; niche aesthetic
parked.docs-to-dbml: narrow; use when a data model is actually the task
parked.likec4-to-openspec: needs a LikeC4 model to exist first
parked.split-tasks-by-profile: team-assignment; solo work does not trigger it
parked.abrege-frere: duplicate of caveman in French — pick one
parked.memory-snapshot-perf: specialist; re-activate when chasing a leak

parked.write-swift: no Swift in the current stack
parked.ask-sonner: one library; re-activate when using Sonner
parked.setup-matt-pocock-skills: installer for a set already installed
parked.find-skills: npx skills find does this from the shell
parked.grill-me: keep grilling — same job, better structure
parked.prototype: two skills share this name; keep one
parked.discernment-nudge: appends follow-up questions to every answer
parked.docx: re-activate when a Word file is the deliverable
parked.xlsx: re-activate when a spreadsheet is the deliverable
parked.pptx: re-activate when a deck is the deliverable
